turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Good morning, madam. Please sit, I will take the vitals before Doctor calls you. The clinic is a bit behind, the previous family came from out of station.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Thank you, sister. I am sorry if I have added to the delay.
[SEG0003] person_1 (NURSE): Not at all. Blood pressure is one thirty over eighty-four. Pulse is ninety-six, a little fast but regular.
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): I did feel warm in the night. I hope it is nothing too serious.

[SEG0005] person_1 (NURSE): Temperature is thirty-eight point four. Saturation is ninety-eight percent on room air. Respiratory rate is eighteen. I will bring Doctor Menon, and we can open the dressing once he is here.
[SEG0006] person_3 (DOCTOR): Mrs. Iyer, good morning. I am Doctor Menon. And you are?
[SEG0007] person_4 (CAREGIVER): Her mother, doctor. I came from Coimbatore last week to help with the baby. The autos were impossible today, that is why we are a little late.
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): Thank you for seeing me, doctor. I do not like to trouble you so soon after the delivery.
[SEG0009] person_3 (DOCTOR): You are not troubling me. The caesarean was ten days ago, yes?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, doctor. Ten days back, lower segment caesarean, at St. Mary's. The baby is well, thank God.
[SEG0011] person_3 (DOCTOR): What has brought you in today, in your own words?
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): The operation wound, doctor. It is red, and there is discharge on the pad. I also had fever in the night.
[SEG0013] person_4 (CAREGIVER): She was shivering near midnight. I wanted to come then itself, but she said morning is more proper.
[SEG0014] person_3 (DOCTOR): Can you tell me when the redness actually started?

[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): I am afraid I cannot date it, doctor. It seems since Diwali or just after, which is absurd, the operation is only ten days old. Then I think of some skin irritation last winter, or the one before, and I mix everything. I simply cannot give you a date.
[SEG0016] person_3 (DOCTOR): We will leave the start date open, then. And the discharge?
[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): That one I can speak for. Yesterday morning the pad had a yellow stain. It is a little more today.
[SEG0018] person_4 (CAREGIVER): Yes, yesterday morning. I changed the pad myself. Before that it was only a pink spot, nothing much.
[SEG0019] person_3 (DOCTOR): Fever only last night, or earlier also?

[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): Only last night, doctor. We did not have a thermometer at home, so I cannot give you a number. It felt high, and then it eased a little towards morning, but I am still warm.
[SEG0021] person_3 (DOCTOR): Pain?
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): A dull pain at the wound. Worse when I walk, or if I cough. If I lie flat it eases. Not severe, I would say, but constant.
[SEG0023] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any vomiting? Loose motions? Burning when you pass urine?
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): No vomiting. Motions are normal. There is no burning.
[SEG0025] person_3 (DOCTOR): And breathlessness, or pain in the chest?
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): Neither, doctor. I am able to speak in full sentences, as you see.
[SEG0027] person_3 (DOCTOR): Medicines. What did they send you home with?

[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): An antibiotic, cefuroxime. Five hundred milligrams, twice daily, by mouth. I took it for five days... or was it seven? I am sorry, I cannot be exact. The course is finished, that much I know.

[SEG0029] person_4 (CAREGIVER): The discharge paper said five days. The strip had fourteen tablets, which is seven days at two a day. She finished the strip. Whether she missed a night or two, I would not swear. I think she did miss some.
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): I did try to take each dose, doctor. I would not wish to mislead you. I cannot prove it either way.
[SEG0031] person_3 (DOCTOR): So cefuroxime five hundred, twice a day, course completed, and the length may be five days or seven, and adherence is not certain. We will not pretend we know. What else?

[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): Thyroxine, seventy-five micrograms, every morning, empty stomach. For the thyroid. It has been five-ish years now. And last night Mother gave me paracetamol, one tablet of a thousand milligrams.

[SEG0033] person_4 (CAREGIVER): Only that one tablet. Also, please, her father takes metformin, five hundred milligrams, for his sugar. I had his strip in my handbag and I nearly offered it. We did not give it.
[SEG0034] person_3 (DOCTOR): Quite right not to. That metformin is his. Any other tablets in the house people have suggested?
[SEG0035] person_4 (CAREGIVER): Her sister-in-law's biotin, for hair fall. It is sitting on the fridge. We have not given even one.
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): I would not take another's medicine, doctor.
[SEG0037] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any allergy to a drug, or a food, that you know of?
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): No, doctor. I have no known allergies.

[SEG0039] person_4 (CAREGIVER): I have to say this. When she was small there was a rash after a syrup. I think it was penicillin. I am not sure of the name, and she has had many courses since without my being there.
[SEG0040] person_2 (PATIENT): Mother, with respect, I do not recall a rash. No doctor has told me I am allergic to anything.
[SEG0041] person_3 (DOCTOR): I hear both of you. I will not call it a confirmed penicillin allergy, and I will not ignore it either. Let me think this through out loud before I touch the wound.

[SEG0042] person_3 (DOCTOR): Ten days after a caesarean, redness, yellow discharge, fever last night, temperature thirty-eight point four now. This could be a stitch reaction, or a superficial infection of the wound, or, less likely, a deeper collection. I am not going to conclude there is an abscess. My leading impression, still provisional, is a superficial surgical site infection.
[SEG0043] person_1 (NURSE): Shall I take the dressing off, doctor?
[SEG0044] person_3 (DOCTOR): Please.

[SEG0045] person_1 (NURSE): Dressing is down. The pad is wet with yellow discharge, more than a smear, not pouring. Redness runs about four centimetres on either side of the incision. At the lower end there is a gap of about one centimetre, with thin fluid. I do not see black skin, and I cannot feel a big pocket.
[SEG0046] person_2 (PATIENT): Oh. It is more angry than it felt. I should have come yesterday. I apologise.

[SEG0047] person_3 (DOCTOR): You are here now. Let me examine. Warm, and tender when I press. No fluctuance, so no obvious pus pocket under the finger. Abdomen above the dressing is soft. The skin is pink-red, not dusky, and I am not calling this a necrotising infection.
[SEG0048] person_4 (CAREGIVER): Doctor, the neighbour made her put turmeric and coconut oil on the edges. Twice only. I told her it was foolish.
[SEG0049] person_2 (PATIENT): It is true, only twice, and I stopped when the discharge increased. I know it was not correct. The neighbour was very insistent, and I was too tired to argue.
[SEG0050] person_3 (DOCTOR): No more oil, no turmeric, no powder. They irritate the skin and they mess up the culture. Keep the wound clean and dry. We will dress it here.
[SEG0051] person_2 (PATIENT): Certainly, doctor. I will follow that.

[SEG0052] person_3 (DOCTOR): I want a wound swab for culture and sensitivity today. Also a blood count and a CRP, in view of the fever. If the report shows a resistant bug we might change the antibiotic later. I am not waiting for the paper to start treatment, and I am not going to pretend the swab result is already known.
[SEG0053] person_2 (PATIENT): Will it sting, the swab?

[SEG0054] person_3 (DOCTOR): A little. About the antibiotic: because of the penicillin question I will not use amoxicillin, and I will not use co-amoxiclav. I am starting cephalexin, five hundred milligrams, by mouth, four times a day, for seven days, after food.
[SEG0055] person_2 (PATIENT): Four times a day. I will keep a written chart so there is no confusion this time. And the thyroxine, I continue as before?

[SEG0056] person_3 (DOCTOR): Yes. Thyroxine seventy-five micrograms every morning, as you have been. Paracetamol, a thousand milligrams, up to three times in a day if there is fever or pain, and not more. You had one last night, so count that in today's total if it was after midnight... actually, last night's dose is last night. From this morning you may take up to three.
[SEG0057] person_4 (CAREGIVER): Doctor, one more thing. My own pressure tablet is amlodipine, five milligrams. If she feels giddy, can she borrow it? It is only five milligrams.
[SEG0058] person_3 (DOCTOR): No. Amlodipine is yours, for your blood pressure, not hers. If she is giddy she should sit, drink some water, and come back, not take your strip.
[SEG0059] person_2 (PATIENT): I understand completely. I will not take Father's metformin or your amlodipine or the biotin.
[SEG0060] person_1 (NURSE): I can swab once you are done, and I will draw the bloods after the swab, before the new pad goes on.

[SEG0061] person_3 (DOCTOR): Thank you, sister. Mrs. Iyer, come back in three days, even if it looks calmer, so I can check the wound and whatever report has come. If the fever goes above thirty-nine, or the redness races outward, or you feel faint, come earlier. Do not wait out the three days.

[SEG0062] person_2 (PATIENT): In three days. May I ask, doctor, is baby Arjun at risk? He is feeding well. The naming function is next month and the priest has phoned twice about the hall, which is a silly worry beside this, I know.

[SEG0063] person_3 (DOCTOR): The hall can wait. Wash your hands before each feed, keep the wound covered, and this is not a reason to stop breastfeeding. I am not his doctor today, but milk itself is not the route I am worried about.
[SEG0064] person_4 (CAREGIVER): She sleeps two hours and then the baby cries. I keep saying rest, rest.
[SEG0065] person_2 (PATIENT): Sleep is broken, yes, but that is the baby, not a new illness, I believe. I am a little tired, that much is fair to say.
[SEG0066] person_3 (DOCTOR): I will note the tiredness. I am not adding a separate diagnosis for the sleep. Any cough, cold, pain in the breasts, swelling of the calves?
[SEG0067] person_2 (PATIENT): No cough and no cold. The breasts are full, not painful in a worrying way. No swelling in the legs.

[SEG0068] person_3 (DOCTOR): Good. Let me say where I have landed, so it is clear. Most likely this is a superficial infection of the caesarean wound. I cannot rule out a small deeper collection. A stitch reaction alone would not usually give a temperature of thirty-eight point four, so that is the less likely of the three. I will not stamp a final label today; the tests still have to help.
[SEG0069] person_2 (PATIENT): I am grateful you explained it, doctor. May I walk about the house?
[SEG0070] person_3 (DOCTOR): Short walks, yes. Do not lift heavier than the baby. Do not sit in a tub. A shower is fine if you pat the wound dry afterwards.
[SEG0071] person_2 (PATIENT): And if the cephalexin makes me sick?

[SEG0072] person_3 (DOCTOR): Take it after food. If you vomit that dose straight away, repeat the one dose. If you cannot keep any tablets down, come back and we might change the route, but only if that happens.
[SEG0073] person_4 (CAREGIVER): The coconut oil is still on the kitchen table. Shall I throw it?
[SEG0074] person_3 (DOCTOR): Yes, throw the idea out, at least. No oil, no turmeric. If the pad leaks, do not stuff a household cloth on it. Come in and we will change the dressing.
[SEG0075] person_1 (NURSE): Madam, I am taking the swab from the lower gap now. It may sting.
[SEG0076] person_2 (PATIENT): Please go ahead, sister. I will manage.

[SEG0077] person_1 (NURSE): Swab is done, from the open lower end. I will send it for culture and sensitivity. I am drawing the blood for the count and the CRP next. Then a simple absorbent dressing, not a tight one.

[SEG0078] person_3 (DOCTOR): That is the plan, then. We still do not have a date for when the redness began, and we still do not know if the cefuroxime was five days or seven. Neither of those stops today's treatment. See you in three days, sooner if those warning signs come. Take care.

spec.situation: Patient 10 days after a hernia, appendix or caesarean operation; wound redness and discharge, fever the night before; nurse removes dressing and describes it; patient is vague about antibiotic course ('five days... or was it seven'); wound swab and antibiotic change.
features: vague_dates: the patient cannot date things ('since Diwali or after', 'last winter, or the one before'); no invented date; a date_uncertain item.

doctor_thinks_aloud: the doctor lists possible causes or says what they will not conclude yet. Only record a clinical assessment if the doctor actually states a leading or differential impression; 'let's see what the tests say' is not an assessment.

third_party_medicine: someone mentions a medicine or condition that belongs to a relative or friend (the sister's biotin, the husband's metformin). It must not appear as the patient's own; a relative's illness can only be family history if said as such.

spoken_numbers: doses, vitals and durations are spoken as words or sloppy speech ('a hundred and two point five', 'one-forty over ninety', 'five-ish years', 'twenty milligram'); the label writes them normally (102.5, 140/90, 20 mg) and does not turn vague ones into exact ones.

bad.reason: Caregiver reports shivering near midnight; 'current' temporality is not supported.
bad.text: shivering (category=constitutional, status=present, onset=around midnight, temporality=current, reported_by=caregiver, certainty=certain)

bad.reason: Doctor ordered 'blood count'; 'complete blood count' not explicitly stated.

omissions.text: Cefuroxime adherence is additionally uncertain because the caregiver said the patient may have missed some night doses, not just that exact duration was 5 vs 7 days.
Cephalexin was specifically instructed to be taken after food.
Thyroxine 75 micrograms was specified to be taken on an empty stomach, and the doctor said to continue it as before.
The patient reported home treatment of the wound with turmeric and coconut oil twice, stopped when discharge increased.
Negative finding: no leg swelling was reported; the recorded fact says 'calf swelling' instead of the patient's broader denial of leg swelling.
Examination: the doctor stated he was not calling this a necrotising infection.
The wound swab was specifically taken from the open lower end/lower gap.
The nurse said bloods would be drawn after the swab and before the new pad/dressing was applied.
